**Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 55, verses 1–2:**

This is the first paragraph in the discussion of the favours of the Most Merciful (Rahman), and it is the first announcement of this general proclamation and its first favour.

*ʿAllama al-Qurʾan* (He taught the Qur'an). Through the teaching of the Qur'an, Allah has bestowed a great mercy upon His servants. The Qur'an is the interpreter of the innate nature (fitrah) of the universe. It is the code (manhaj) of the heavens for the inhabitants of the earth, and this code connects the inhabitants of the earth with the laws of nature (nawamis-i-fitrah). It firmly establishes their beliefs, their concepts, their standards, their values, their institutions and their conditions upon the most solid foundations, the very foundations upon which this entire universe stands. This constitution grants them ease, tranquillity, and harmony and reconciliation with the laws of nature.

The Qur'an opens the perceptions and the consciousness of humanity toward this entire universe, saying: "Look, how beautiful this universe is." The Qur'an makes them observe it in such a way that it is as if humanity were seeing the universe for the first time. They had seen it before, but this is a new contemplation. They also re-examined their own selves. They began to read the universe around them. Rather, the Qur'an gave life to this whole cosmic environment, and this environment began to move alongside humanity. Now the human being became a friend and companion of the phenomena of this universe, and they walk together as companions, and the human journey upon this earth began to proceed with great joy.

This Qur'an made humanity realise that: "O humankind! You are the vicegerents (khulafa') of Allah in this universe, the vicegerents of the Most Merciful. You are highly honoured in the sight of Allah. Allah has given you this Qur'an as a great trust (amanah), the trust which the heavens, the earth and the mountains declined to bear." Understand the worth and value of the lofty humanity that the Qur'an grants you, and this understanding and perception is possible only through the Qur'an, and possible only through the path of faith. Faith alone can breathe into your soul this spirit and this guidance, and only through the Qur'an can you attain the great blessing of Allah. This is why Allah, before mentioning the creation of humankind and the blessings of bringing them into existence, mentioned teaching, because it is through the teaching of the Qur'an that a human being can become truly human.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 55, verses 3–4:

Khalaqa al-insan (55:3), 'allamahu al-bayan (55:4): (He created man and taught him speech.)

We are not discussing here the blessing of the creation of man; that will come shortly in the surah. Here the main purpose is the mention of teaching.

We see that man speaks. He expresses what is in his mind (ma fi al-damir). He explains, understands the words of others, and then humans cooperate with one another. Since this activity is constantly taking place among us, we have forgotten this greatest blessing of Allah; otherwise, if one reflects even a little, it is a wonder. The Qur'an reminds us of many such blessings and wakes us up.

What is man? What is his reality? How is this speech taught to him? The reality of man is that he is a cell that is present in the father's seminal fluid. It begins its life in the womb in a very simple form. It is very small and weak. It is so small that it can be seen only through instruments; it is not visible, and it cannot express itself.

This cell soon takes the form of a foetus. In this foetus the number of cells again becomes several million. Bone cells, cartilage cells, muscle cells, nerve cells and skin cells. Then organs are formed, and the amazing functions and capacities of these organs: hearing, seeing, tasting, smelling and touching, and then consciousness and inspiration. All these cells and all these properties were formed from that one cell, which was a simple cell, extremely small, which was not visible and could not express itself.

How did this happen? Whence did it come? It comes from the Most Merciful (al-Rahman); it is one of the creations of the Most Merciful.

Consider carefully how Allah taught this creature speech.

﴿وَاللَّهُ أَخْرَجَكُم مِّن بُطُونِ أُمَّهَاتِكُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ شَيْئًا وَجَعَلَ لَكُمُ السَّمْعَ وَالْأَبْصَارَ وَالْأَفْئِدَةَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ﴾ (16:78) (Allah brought you forth from your mothers' wombs knowing nothing, and He gave you hearing, sight and hearts, that you may give thanks.)

The truth is that the organs of speech are themselves that wonder whose wonders can never be exhausted. The tongue, lips, face, teeth, windpipe, larynx and lungs all take part in it. All these organs participate in producing sound, and this function of the organs becomes the basis of speech. In this intricate process these organs display the working of a mechanism. After this, these organs are connected to the brain, the faculty of hearing and the whole nervous system. Then they are connected to the intellect, and what the intellect is, we know only that it is called "intellect." We do not know its essence and reality, nor do we know how the intellect works.

When a speaker utters a word, how does he utter it? It is a process that has many stages, many levels and many instruments, and some of its aspects are still not known.

First, the awareness arises that this word should be spoken for this purpose. This awareness comes from the intellect, the faculty of perception or the soul to the sensory instruments. How it comes, we do not know. Regarding the brain, it is said that it commands, through the nerves, the aforementioned instruments to pronounce this word. What is this word in itself? It is the sound that Allah taught to every human and taught its meanings. Now the lungs transfer a quantity of air through a passage to the windpipe. Then this air comes to the throat. Here is the system of cords that produces sound. This system is very different from and more complex than the strings of the sound instruments made by humans. Nor can the instruments made by man that produce sound resemble this system. After this, sound is produced in the larynx, and after that the sound is shaped as the intellect desires: high sound, soft sound, low sound, sharp sound, thick sound, harsh sound, gentle sound, thin sound, in short every kind of sound. Then the tongue, lips, jaws and teeth work together with the larynx. As a result of pressure from different parts, letters are formed, and the place from which they emerge is their makhraj (point of articulation). The tongue has the marvel that it produces each letter from a particular part of itself, which has a specific effect. The tongue concentrates the pressure on that part. Likewise, a specific melody arises in the sound of the letters.

All these instruments merely arrange the pronunciation of a single word. After that, the composition of the topic, thoughts, feelings, past and new; in short, this system, the "system of speech" (nizam bayan), is itself a miracle. This speech has been placed within the human body. It is an attribute of the Most Merciful and a bounty of the Most Merciful.

Now, within this exhibition of the cosmos, two further wonders fashioned by the hand of divine power.

﴿The sun and the moon follow a precise reckoning.﴾ (55:5) Upon observing the structure, movement and harmony of the sun and the moon, a person is left amazed and astonished. It becomes evident that this is a grand system, that it points to the greatness of the One who organises it, that profound truths lie hidden within this system, and that the consequences that flow from it are far-reaching.

The sun is not the largest of the celestial bodies. In this cosmos, whose boundaries man has not been able to determine, there are several million stars, many of which are larger than the sun and have greater heat and more intense light. Some are twenty times larger and hotter, and their light is fifty times brighter than the light of the sun.

Sirius (al-Shi'ra al-Yamani) is twenty times heavier than the sun, and its light is fifty times greater than the sun's light. Arcturus (Simak Ra'ih) has a volume eighty times that of the sun's volume, and its light is eight thousand times brighter. The volume of Canopus (Suhayl) is two thousand five hundred times greater than the sun. And likewise are other stars and planets.

Yet for us the sun is the more important, that is, for us the inhabitants of the earth, because this earth, its present condition and human life depend upon the sun's heat, and the sun's gravitational pull also plays a great role in this.

Likewise the moon, which is a small satellite of this earth, nevertheless holds importance in the life of this earth. The tides within the seas arise because of it.

The size of the sun, its temperature, its distance from us, its circling in its orbit, and likewise the size of the moon, its distance from us and its revolution in its orbit: all these matters are fashioned by extremely precise calculations and measurements, and they affect the life of the earth, in comparison with the other stars and planets. We record here some calculations of the sun and moon, so that you may see that if there were even the slightest variation in these calculations with respect to the earth, far-reaching consequences would follow.

The sun is 529,000 miles away from the earth. If it were closer, the earth would burn and all water would turn into vapour, and the vapours would rise into the atmosphere; and if it were a little farther away, all things would freeze. The heat that reaches us from the sun is one part in two million of its heat, and this modest heat is sufficient for our present life. If Sirius, with its present volume and heat, were in the place of the sun, the whole earth would burn to ash and the water would turn to vapour and scatter into the celestial atmosphere.

Likewise the size of the moon and its distance from us have been set according to a measure. If it were even a little larger, the storms within the sea would be so great that the earth would be repeatedly submerged. Likewise, if it were closer to us, that is, nearer than where it is, it would still create storms upon the earth; but at the place where Allah has set it, it does not deviate even by a hair's breadth.

The gravitational pull of the sun and the moon is fixed for the earth at a particular measure, and their motion too has been arranged according to a most firm calculation. Our entire galaxy and solar system is moving in one direction at a speed of about twenty thousand miles per hour, and in this course it has not collided with any other star, and several million years have passed in this motion, and the expanse of the cosmos has not come to an end.

Within this vast celestial expanse, no star deviates from its orbit even by a hair's breadth, and the balance and harmony established between them undergoes no change in their volume or in their motion. The Divine Being has spoken truly:

﴿And the stars and the trees prostrate themselves.﴾ (55:6) The preceding indication was that a firm reckoning has been placed in the creation and formation of this cosmos, and this indication points to the fact that this entire cosmos is bound to the Being of Allah. That it moves in accordance with the directions of the Exalted Lord and is obedient to Him. The meaning is that this cosmos is wholly obedient to Allah, just as a servant and slave is obedient, and it acknowledges the laws that the Creator has set for it. The stars and the trees are examples of this servitude and obedience. Some have understood "the star" to mean the star that is in the sky, while others have taken "the tree" to mean the grass that does not stand upon a stalk. Whatever the meaning, the sense of the verse remains the same: the obedience and servitude of all things is directed towards Allah.

In short, this cosmos is a creation having one soul, and its forms, manifestations and degrees of that soul differ. In each thing there is a certain soul, and in another a soul of a different kind, but in reality the soul of the cosmos is one.

The human heart perceived the soul of the cosmos long ago, and that this entire cosmos, by reason of its soul, turns towards its Creator. Every person was made aware of this truth through inspiration from the presence of God; but when man sought to know that soul through his senses, this truth, this inspired truth, was clouded over and became hidden from human sight. Whenever an attempt was made to know this truth through the four legs of reason, it fled.

Recently man has discovered a part of the signs of unity in the creation of the cosmos, but present materialistic humanity has not been able to reach the soul of the cosmos, which is a living soul, and it can only be reached in a spiritual manner, and it can indeed be reached.

Scientists begin their work by holding that the particle is the first unit of creation, that it is composed solely of radiation or light, that motion is the principle of the cosmos, and that there is a common characteristic of motion among all the bodies and individuals of the cosmos.

The questions, indeed the questions, are: where is this cosmos going while in motion? That is a quality and property of the cosmos. The Noble Qur'an informs us that this cosmos is turned towards its Creator, and that this is true motion. Apparent motion is in reality an expression of the motion of the soul of the cosmos, and the Noble Qur'an expresses the motion of this soul of the cosmos in such words.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 55, verse 6:

﴿And the star and the tree prostrate themselves.﴾ (55:6) (The stars and the trees are prostrating.) This has been expressed in some other verses as well.

﴿The seven heavens and the earth and whatever is in them glorify Him. And there is not a thing but that it exalts His praise, but you do not understand their glorification.﴾ (71:44) (His purity is being declared by the seven heavens and the earth and by everything in them as well. There is nothing which does not glorify Him with His praise, but you do not understand their glorification.) And elsewhere:

﴿Do you not see that to Allah prostrate whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and the birds in flight, each one knows its prayer and its glorification?﴾ (24:41) (Do you not see that all who are in the heavens and the earth are glorifying Allah, and the birds spreading their wings in flight? Each one knows its own manner of prayer and glorification.)

When a person reflects on the reality that the whole universe is in prostration and is engaged in praising and glorifying Allah, the human heart receives a great provision for reaching the Divine Presence. He regards his surroundings as alive, loves them, and, walking in step with them, turns in flight toward Allah. This thought, this companionship with the soul of the universe, makes a person a friend of this universe.

This is an extremely far-reaching allusion and very profound.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 55, verse 7:

﴿And the heaven He raised high, and He set up the balance﴾ (55:7-9)

(He raised the heaven and set up the balance. Its requirement is that you do not disturb the balance; weigh with justice, with correct and exact measure, and do not cheat in the scale.) Here the reference is to the heaven. Like the other indications in the Qur'an, this too is meant to awaken heedless hearts, and the aim is to draw attention to the fact that you see the heaven by night and by day, so do not lose its significance. Reflect on it: on its greatness, its beauty, and its quality of being a balance, that in its orbits and its motion not even a hair's breadth of difference occurs, and through it behold the powers of the Possessor of power.

Whatever is meant by "heaven," here it is commanded: just look upward; above you is a terrifying expanse, very high and very far, without bounds or limits. Within that expanse, thousands of millions of enormous celestial bodies are floating. Not one of them collides with another. Their clusters do not strike against other clusters. The number of stars in a single cluster sometimes reaches a thousand million stars. The cluster to which our solar system is attributed contains bodies like our sun, and bodies many thousands of times larger. The diameter of our sun alone is 21 million kilometres. All these stars and all these clusters are moving within this universe with an extremely frightening speed, yet all of them are in this great and awe-inspiring, vast expanse of the cosmos in the way that particles float in the earth's atmosphere, moving far from one another, without any collision among them. (And if it were to happen, then what?)

Just as Allah has raised this heaven, and made it terrifyingly vast, and has appointed for it a natural balance, so too has He appointed for you a balance of truth. It is established, firm and fixed. And this balance is for measuring and weighing values: the worth of individuals, the worth of events, the worth of things, so that everyone's weight and value may be determined, no disturbance may occur in them, and people do not go about judging good and bad according to ignorance, prejudice and desires. This balance is placed within human nature, and also within the Islamic call which all the Messengers brought, and which at last came in the form of the Qur'an.

Allah has established the balance (mizan). Its requirement is that:

*Alla tatghaw fi al-mizan* (55:8) "Do not transgress in the balance; do not cause a deficiency or an excess. And *wa aqimu al-wazna bil-qist wa la tukhsiru al-mizan* ..." "Establish the weight with justice, and do not give short measure in the balance; weigh with true and exact justice, and do not cheat with the scale." The balance is established so that rights are given to those who deserve them and justice is done; therefore neither go beyond the limit nor fall short of it.

In this way, between the truth and the balance that exist in the earth, and the rights that exist in human life, there will be a balance and harmony, by giving each right to its rightful claimant, between the Islamic order and the order of the universe. Thus, between the descent of revelation from the heavens and the exalted height of the heavens, Allah's balance operates, and thus these two meanings overshadow human consciousness.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 55, verses 10–12:

﴿And the earth He has set out for the creatures.﴾ (55:10) ﴿In it are fruits, and palm trees with sheaths (of their spathes).﴾ (55:11) ﴿And grain with its husk, and fragrant herbs.﴾ (55:12)

(The earth was made by Him for His creatures. In it are fruits of every kind in abundance, there are date palms whose fruit is wrapped in sheaths, and there are various kinds of grain, containing both chaff and kernel.)

We do not notice these things, living and dwelling upon this earth again and again. Seeing the conditions and ways of this earth, and seeing our own conditions and circumstances at every moment, we find nothing in it that is unusual, which in truth would be a wonder and a marvellous work of the hand of divine power. We have not come to appreciate the technology by which we are kept in such peace and stability upon the earth, nor have we understood the meaning of how we are kept settled here; otherwise we would form some conception of the power and greatness of God. Yes, occasionally, when there is volcanic activity or a severe earthquake, the earth trembles beneath our feet; then we feel some unease, and understand what it means for the earth to be obedient.

This is the duty of human beings, and it is fitting for them to remember this at all times. If they pay some attention to this earth upon which they walk and run, they will see that it is merely a speck floating in this terrifying and awe-inspiring, vast expanse of space. It is in this absolute, unbounded, limitless space. This speck itself also spins around its own axis at a speed of one thousand miles per hour, and around the sun it moves at a speed of sixty thousand miles per hour, while this earth, this sun, and their whole star system are moving at a speed of about twenty thousand miles per hour in some direction that we do not know. Scientists say that they are moving toward the constellation Virgo (Burj Jiyar).

Yes, if human beings reflect on the fact that they are riding upon a tiny speck, and that this speck is racing through that space at such speed, and that it hangs in that space with no pillar or support, merely held thus by the hand of divine power, then they would always carry the fear of God within their hearts, trembling and quaking, and turn their attention solely to the One who keeps it so, while they go about upon this exceedingly swift steed.

God has indeed provided in it the means of life for this fear. They eat and drink within it, while it carries them along, running around itself, running around the sun, and running along with the whole solar system. And then within this very earth God has created our sustenance, fruits and provisions, and tall date palms whose fruit is enclosed in sheaths.

(Kamm/Akmam is the name for the sheath or covering from which the date fruit emerges; it is somewhat beautiful.) Then there are other clustered crops and grains which have chaff upon them, and when the chaff is removed and the grains extracted, the grains are for human beings and the chaff is for livestock. Here the mention of Rayhan is also made: some plants are fragrant, and upon the earth there are various kinds of plants which are fragrant; some of these fragrant plants are food for human beings, some are food for animals, and some are merely fragrances which are a means of enjoyment of life for human beings.

After the mention of these bounties of God, namely the teaching of the Qur'an, the teaching of expression, the orderly movement of the sun and moon, the heights of the heavens and the balance of the heavens, the balance among the people of the earth, the earth being kept firm for people, and the fruits, produce and fragrances within it, both outwardly and inwardly beautiful, having enumerated these favours and kindnesses, the address is made to both jinn and humankind, the two communities charged with religious obligation.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 55, verses 14–15:

"He created man from clay like pottery, and He created the jinn from a smokeless flame of fire. So which of the favours of your Lord would you both deny?"

Creation and bringing into existence are among the foundations of blessing. The gaps between existence and non-existence cannot be measured by any of the measures that lie within human perception. This is because the measures within human reach, or those that human minds have grasped, are measures for distinguishing one existent from another existent. As for the difference between existence and non-existence, and how great the distances are, humans cannot know these. The same is true of the jinn; their measures too are the measures of created beings.

When Allah reminds humans and jinn that I have brought you from non-existence into existence, this is a blessing that lies beyond the limits of perception. After this it is explained that the creation of man was from a material, and the creation of the jinn was from a material.

Man was created by Allah from ṣalṣāl (55:4 1). Ṣalṣāl refers to clay that has dried, such that when struck it produces the sound ṣalṣala. It is possible that this was one stage in the process of man's creation from clay, and it is also possible that it means there is no difference between the material of man's creation and the material of clay.

"Modern science has proved that within the human body there is the same material as within the clay. Man is composed of carbon, oxygen, hydrogen, phosphorus, sulphur, calcium, potassium, sodium chloride, magnesium, iron, manganese, copper, lead, fluorine, cobalt, zinc, silicon and aluminium, and these are the very elements from which the earth is made. Although the proportion of these within a human being differs, and the proportion differs between a human and the clay, the elements and kinds are one and the same." ("Allah aur Science", p. 081)

But what science has stated does not necessarily mean that this is the interpretation of the verse. It is possible that the Quran's meaning is what science has established, or it is something that scientists do not yet know and is something else. Or it may be that man is called "empty creation" in another sense, and ṭīn and ṣalṣāl have some other meanings.

What we have strongly warned against is that a verse should not be confined to the concepts discovered by modern science, because human discoveries may be correct or incorrect and are subject to change and alteration. As human knowledge grows, human theories change and are transformed. Some sincere people quickly try to make Quranic verses conform to scientific concepts, whether these concepts are experimental or hypothetical, and their intention is to prove the miraculousness of the Quran. This is because the Quran, whether it agrees or disagrees with science, is a miracle in its own right. The meanings of the Quran's texts are very broad and cannot be limited to the discoveries of a single era, because these discoveries always carry the possibility of error, and sometimes theories are entirely shown to be false. From modern scientific information we can only benefit to the extent that through them we broaden our conception of the meaning and implication of verses, provided they point toward the meanings to which the Quran points. But we never claim that the Quran's meaning is exactly what our discoveries have reached. The permissible claim is only that we may say: this is that thing to which the Quran has also pointed.

As for the question of whether the jinn were created from a flame of fire, this matter lies beyond the limits of human knowledge. The Quran has only informed us of the existence of the jinn, and has also stated that they were created from fire. Ṃārij means the tongue-like smokeless flame of fire, which is formed from wind. As for how the jinn and their progeny live on this earth alongside humans, we do not have knowledge of this. The certain matter is that they are obliged to act upon the Quran and the Shariah, as we have explained earlier.

In the commentary on "wa idh ṣarafnā ilaika nafaran mina al-jinni yastamiʿūna al-Qurʾān" (And recall when We turned towards you a group of the jinn who were listening to the Quran), it was said that both jinn and humans are addressed in this verse, asking which of Allah's blessings they would deny. Both were created by Allah, and creating and granting existence is the blessing upon which all other blessings depend. Accordingly, this testimony is established upon this entire paragraph.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 55, verses 19–21:

"He released the two seas, meeting side by side; between them is a barrier which they do not transgress. So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny? From them emerge pearls and coral. So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny? And His are the ships, towering like mountains on the sea. So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?"

Here, the two seas referred to are the sweet sea and the salt sea. By the salt sea is meant the sea and large, deep waters, and by the sweet is meant the smaller rivers. They meet, yet neither of them goes beyond its prescribed limits. Each does not transgress its boundaries, and between them is a barrier.

This division of waters on the surface of the earth did not happen by chance. It is the arrangement of Allah's providence, set with a profound and precise measure. Salt water spreads over 3/4 of the surface of the earth, and only 1/4 is dry land, and these lands are contiguous with one another. Such a vast expanse of saline water is very essential for the surface of the earth, so that it keeps the earth clean and remains suitable for the growth of life.

"Gases continuously emerge from the earth. They have been emerging for ages, and most of them are poisonous, but the air is not polluted by these gases. Nor does the ratio of the components of the air that is necessary for human existence change. The guarantor of maintaining this balance is that great reservoir of water, namely the sea." (1)

When the sun shines upon this great reservoir of water, vapours rise from it, and from these vapours clouds and rains are formed, and from them sweet-water rivers flow over the dry land. The sea, solar heat, the cold of the upper atmosphere and other astronomical factors together produce rain, and from these the sweet sea is formed.

Upon this sweet water depends the life of humans, animals and plants. All rivers go and fall into the seas and carry the salt of the earth down into the sea, yet they cannot spoil the waters of the sea. The surface of every river is higher than the surface of the sea. Therefore the sea cannot lay a hand upon these rivers, since these rivers fall into the sea itself. Along the paths on which these rivers flow, the salt water does not intrude, nor can salt water prevent these clean waters from doing their work. There is a barrier between the two, so the mention of two seas and the barrier between them is nothing to be surprised at. "So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?"

After this comes the mention of Allah's favours found in the seas, especially those things which are close to their practical life.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 55, verses 76–77:

Reclining on ﴿green cushions and beautiful, rare carpets﴾ (55:76). The passage reads: "They will recline on green cushions and beautiful, rare carpets." (55:67 is cited here as well.)

Rafraf are carpets woven from ʿabqarī (ʿabqar), meaning that they are such that people, especially the Arabs, are made to understand the matter through familiar imagery. ʿAbqar (the valley of the jinn) is what they called it, and they used the term ʿabqarī (ʿabqarī, "masterful, extraordinary") for every wondrous thing. However, the cushions of the people of the first two gardens were lined with istabraq (thick silk brocade). Therefore there will be a difference in rank between the people of the first two gardens and the people of the other two gardens. And after all these attributes and perfections, the statement follows: ﴿Then which of the favours of your Lord will you deny, O jinn and humankind?﴾ (55:77)

The mention of Allah's blessings in this universe, the mention of Allah's blessings among creatures, and the mention of Allah's blessings in the Hereafter was the theme of this surah. Now, at its end, comes the final lesson and the final conclusion: glorify Allah, acknowledge the bounties of Allah, for it is He who causes every living thing to die, and He alone will remain.
